predictions.title: FMRB executive order signs inside the OECD GENAI plenary window by June 6 2026
predictions.body: By the close of the OECD GENAI June 2-6 plenary the Frontier Model Review Board executive order is signed inside the plenary window itself, with OSTP exercising the now-open post-deadline signing window on a date that falls between the plenary's opening session and its final closing read, and the sixteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter formally recognizing the United States as the seventeenth named jurisdiction in the same plenary's closing session rather than deferring the recognition into a post-plenary written-procedure round. The Friday catalysts trace a clean convergence of three previously-independent regulatory clocks landing inside a single pre-weekend operating session. A Friday Lawfare procedural note reports the classified-annex response clock reaching its T-zero May 22 deadline window with the National Security Agency Director, the Federal Bureau of Investigation Cyber Division Assistant Director, and the Office of Management and Budget Federal Chief Information Officer all filing substantive responses during the Friday morning intake window, lifting the witness count to eight of eight on record and clearing the last open procedural gate inside the deadline window itself; OSTP shifts its posture from the prior 'no signing window before May 22' line to 'signing window open from end-of-day May 22 forward' as the post-deadline session opens. A Friday Just Security analysis observes that an eight-of-eight close inside the deadline window itself is the cleanest reading of the response curve the eight-witness slate could have produced and frames the post-deadline signing window as a near-term plenary-window arithmetic rather than a forward-looking question. A Friday andrew.ooo procedural note confirms the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat reporting that member-state delegations entered the second business day of the working-procedure review on the draft Recommendation text, with all sixteen named candidates plus the originating UK and EU now confirmed in active delegation review and the plenary now at T-minus-eleven calendar days and T-minus-seven business days. A Friday Decoder note reports the named-candidate count holding at sixteen with the cohort treating the now-eight-of-eight Senate classified-annex close on the United States side as the first concrete signal that the FMRB executive order signing window can in fact open inside the June 2-6 plenary horizon, converting the United States recognition-gap closure from a forward-looking question into a near-term plenary-window arithmetic. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology held its Thursday-locked Wednesday May 27 morning markup slot on the parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft and circulated a Friday-morning supplemental staff memorandum to committee members covering the now-closed Senate classified-annex record, and a Friday CSO Online note confirms the CISA federal-civilian operational directive transitioning into its compliance-monitoring phase at T-zero on the same Friday session — giving the executive order a settled operational precedent it can cite in its preamble. The structural force is that once the eight-of-eight classified-annex slate closes inside the May 22 deadline window with OSTP shifting to a post-deadline signing-window-open posture, the OECD GENAI working-procedure review enters its second business day with sixteen named candidates plus the originating UK and EU all in active delegation review eleven calendar days out from the plenary, the House parallel-track joint resolution holds its locked May 27 subcommittee markup slot with a Friday-morning supplemental staff memorandum circulated, and the CISA federal-civilian operational directive transitions into compliance-monitoring mode the same Friday session, the three regulatory clocks compress into a single coincident inflection window rather than three independent forward-looking schedules — and the path of least resistance lands the executive order signed inside the June 2-6 plenary window with the sixteen-jurisdiction perimeter recognizing the United States in the plenary's closing session itself. The most likely landing is the executive order signing between the OECD plenary's opening session on June 2 and its closing read on June 6, the sixteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter formally recognizing the United States as the seventeenth named jurisdiction in the plenary's closing session, the parallel House Energy and Commerce joint resolution clearing its May 27 subcommittee markup inside the run-up and advancing to full-committee markup inside Q3 2026, and the CISA federal-civilian compliance-monitoring directive cited as the operational precedent inside the order's preamble. Bear case is that one of the secretariat's working-procedure review business days raises a fresh comment chapter that pushes the plenary closing-session recognition vote into the four-week-following written-procedure round with the executive order signing still landing inside the plenary window itself; absent that slip, June 6 2026 lands the executive order signed inside the OECD GENAI plenary window with the sixteen-jurisdiction perimeter recognizing the United States in the same closing session.

reasoning.because: June 2 cyber EO signed in the plenary window, designating covered frontier models (proxy, not FMRB).
reasoning.given: Signing leg satisfied; OECD sixteen-jurisdiction-plus-UK/EU recognition of the US is the open leg.
reasoning.so_that: The OECD GENAI perimeter recognizes the US on the now-live oversight stack, not a later written-procedure round.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; sixteen jurisdictions plus UK and EU formally recognize the US.
reasoning.plain_language: The US AI order was signed in June; now sixteen countries still have to formally recognize it.

predictions.summary: Friday closes the FMRB classified-annex slate eight-of-eight inside the May 22 deadline window and OSTP opens its post-deadline signing posture, with the OECD GENAI plenary at T-minus-eleven days. By June 6 2026 the executive order signs inside the plenary window.
